subject: maths
title: Order of Operations (BODMAS / BIDMAS)
seo_title: Year 6 Order of Operations Worksheets: BODMAS, BIDMAS and Brackets
standard_code: Year 6: Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division
standard_text: Use their knowledge of the order of operations to carry out calculations involving the four operations; perform mental calculations, including with mixed operations and large numbers; use estimation to check answers to calculations and determine, in the context of a problem, an appropriate degree of accuracy.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on the order of operations: BODMAS and BIDMAS, brackets, squares, working left to right, mental calculation with large numbers and estimating to check. 100 SATs-style questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Brackets first, then squares and cubes, then × and ÷, then + and −: 5 + 3 × 4 = 5 + 12 = 17.
key_sub: × and ÷ are equals, so work from left to right: 48 ÷ 6 × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16. + and − work the same way: 20 − 8 + 3 = 15.
body_html:
Why the order matters

A calculation with more than one operation can give different answers if people work in a different order. So everyone uses the same order. In England it is often called BODMAS or BIDMAS.

StepDo thisExample
1Brackets(25 + 15) × 3 = 40 × 3 = 120
2Indices: squares and cubes32 + 4 = 9 + 4 = 13
3Division and Multiplication, as equals, from left to right48 ÷ 6 × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16
4Addition and Subtraction, as equals, from left to right20 − 8 + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15

D comes before M in the word, but they are equals. Do whichever comes first from the left. A and S work the same way.

Worked examples

Brackets first

Calculate (25 + 15) × 3.

(25 + 15) × 3 = 40 × 3 = 120. Without the brackets, 25 + 15 × 3 = 25 + 45 = 70.

Answer: 120

Squares

Calculate 32 + 4.

32 means 3 × 3 = 9 (not 3 × 2). So 32 + 4 = 9 + 4 = 13.

Answer: 13

One calculation for a word problem

3 drinks cost 85p each and a sandwich costs £2.40. What is the total?

Write it in pence: 3 × 85 + 240 = 255 + 240 = 495p.

Answer: £4.95

Estimate to check

Round each number to make an easy calculation. 4,987 × 21 is about 5,000 × 20 = 100,000. If your answer is near 10,000 or 1,000,000, check it again. In a problem, think about what the answer means: if 1,030 people travel on coaches with 49 seats, 1,030 ÷ 49 = 21 r 1, so 22 coaches are needed.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
5 + 3 × 4 = 8 × 4 = 32Multiply first: 5 + 12 = 17
48 ÷ 6 × 2 = 48 ÷ 12 = 4÷ and × are equals: left to right, 8 × 2 = 16
20 − 8 + 3 = 20 − 11 = 9+ and − are equals: left to right, 12 + 3 = 15
32 = 3 × 2 = 632 = 3 × 3 = 9
(25 + 15) × 3 = 25 + 45 = 70Work out the brackets first: 40 × 3 = 120

faq.a: It is a way to remember the order of operations: Brackets, Orders or Indices (squares and cubes), Division and Multiplication, then Addition and Subtraction. For example, 5 + 3 × 4 = 5 + 12 = 17.

faq.q: Do you always divide before you multiply in BIDMAS?
faq.a: No. Division and multiplication are equals, so you work from left to right. 48 ÷ 6 × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16. Addition and subtraction work the same way: 20 − 8 + 3 = 15.

faq.q: Is the order of operations in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. It is part of the Year 6 National Curriculum, so calculations such as (25 + 15) × 3 or 500 + 7 × 20 can appear in the arithmetic paper (Paper 1) and in reasoning questions.

faq.q: How do you use estimation to check an answer?
faq.a: Round each number so the calculation is easy, then compare. 4,987 × 21 is about 5,000 × 20 = 100,000, so an answer like 10,473 must be wrong.

sets.title: Multiply and divide before you add and subtract

items.e: 7 + 2 × 5 = 7 + 10 = 17. 45 comes from adding first. 10 stops after 2 × 5. 19 is 7 × 2 + 5, the wrong pair.
48 ÷ 6 + 2 × 4 = 8 + 2 × 4 = 8 + 8 = 16. Not 40: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
45 − 18 ÷ 3 + 6 = 45 − 6 + 6 = 39 + 6 = 45. Not 15: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.

items.q: Which part of 40 − 30 ÷ 5 do you work out first?
items.e: 40 − 30 ÷ 5 = 40 − 6 = 34. Divide before you subtract.
4 × 8 + 9 = 32 + 9 = 41. Not 68: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing.
300 + 50 × 8 = 300 + 400 = 700. Not 2,800: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
7 × 6 + 9 × 4 = 42 + 9 × 4 = 42 + 36 = 78. Not 204: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
7 × 10 − 2 × 4 = 70 − 2 × 4 = 70 − 8 = 62. Not 272: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
78 − 5 × 6 + 16 = 78 − 30 + 16 = 48 + 16 = 64. Not 454: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
7 × 5 − 2 = 35 − 2 = 33. Not 21: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing.
7 + 6 × 2 = 7 + 12 = 19. Not 26: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
90 ÷ 6 − 4 = 15 − 4 = 11. Not 45: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing.
28 + 6 ÷ 2 = 28 + 3 = 31. Not 17: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
22 + 8 × 11 = 22 + 88 = 110. Not 330: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
36 − 24 ÷ 3 = 36 − 8 = 28. Not 4: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
18 − 12 ÷ 3 = 18 − 4 = 14. 2 comes from subtracting first. 22 adds the 4 instead of subtracting it. 6 is just 18 − 12.
79 − 3 × 6 = 79 − 18 = 61. Not 456: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
3 + 5 × 6 − 4 = 3 + 30 − 4 = 33 − 4 = 29. Not 44: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
55 ÷ 5 + 6 = 11 + 6 = 17. Not 5: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing.

items.q: Which part of 4 + 6 × 3 do you work out first?
items.e: 4 + 6 × 3 = 4 + 18 = 22. Multiply before you add.
(53 − 8) × 3 = 45 × 3 = 135. Not 29: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
(5 + 8) × (10 − 6) = 13 × (10 − 6) = 13 × 4 = 52. Not 79: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
72 ÷ (4 × 2) = 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Not 36: that comes from ignoring the brackets.

items.q: Which part of (9 − 4) × 6 do you work out first?
items.e: (9 − 4) × 6 = 5 × 6 = 30. Brackets come first, even though × usually comes before −.
3 + (15 − 2) × 4 = 3 + 13 × 4 = 3 + 52 = 55. Not 10: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
(56 − 20) ÷ (4 + 2) = 36 ÷ (4 + 2) = 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Not 53: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
7 × (8 + 4) = 7 × 12 = 84. Not 60: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
5 × (12 − 3) = 5 × 9 = 45. Not 57: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
5 × (7 + 2 × 3) = 5 × (7 + 6) = 5 × 13 = 65. Not 41: that comes from ignoring the brackets.

items.q: Which part of 50 − (12 + 8) × 2 do you work out first?

items.e: 24 ÷ (6 − 2) = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Not 2: that comes from ignoring the brackets.

items.q: Which calculation has the same value as 6 + 4 × 5?
items.e: 6 + 4 × 5 = 6 + 20 = 26. The brackets in 6 + (4 × 5) show what you do first anyway, so the value stays 26. (6 + 4) × 5 = 50, 6 × (4 + 5) = 54 and 6 × 4 + 5 = 29.
(27 − 9) ÷ 3 = 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Not 24: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
(4 + 5) × 3 = 9 × 3 = 27. Not 19: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
77 − (7 + 8) = 77 − 15 = 62. Not 78: that comes from ignoring the brackets.

items.q: Which calculation has a different value from the others?
items.e: 7 × (4 + 2) = 7 × 6 = 42. The other three all equal 7 × 4 + 2 = 28 + 2 = 30, because × is done before + anyway.
6 × (7 + 9) − 2 = 6 × 16 − 2 = 96 − 2 = 94. Not 49: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
(30 + 18) ÷ 6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Not 33: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
87 − 6 × (12 − 5) = 87 − 6 × 7 = 87 − 42 = 45. Not 10: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
(35 + 5) × 3 = 40 × 3 = 120. Not 50: that comes from ignoring the brackets.
3 × 4<sup>2</sup> = 3 × 16 = 48. Not 144: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.
78 − 16 − 10 + 5 = 62 − 10 + 5 = 52 + 5 = 57. Not 77: that comes from working from right to left.

items.q: Which part of 48 ÷ 6 × 2 do you work out first?
items.e: 48 ÷ 6 × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16. ÷ and × are equals, so work from left to right. Doing 6 × 2 first gives 48 ÷ 12 = 4, which is wrong.
12 + 48 ÷ 3 × 4 = 12 + 16 × 4 = 12 + 64 = 76. Not 16: that comes from multiplying before dividing, but × and ÷ are equals, so work from left to right.

42 − 12 − 2 = 30 − 2 = 28. Not 32: that comes from working from right to left.

24 ÷ 3 × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16. Not 4: that comes from multiplying before dividing, but × and ÷ are equals, so work from left to right.

items.q: Which part of 20 − 8 + 3 do you work out first?
items.e: 20 − 8 + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15. + and − are equals, so work from left to right. Doing 8 + 3 first gives 20 − 11 = 9, which is wrong.
8<sup>2</sup> − 5 × 3 = 64 − 5 × 3 = 64 − 15 = 49. Not 177: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.

sets.title: Place the brackets, and mental calculation with large numbers

items.q:
Where do the brackets go to make this true?
100 − 30 − 20 + 10 = 40
Zara says (25 + 15) × 3 = 120. Kai says it is 70. Who is right?
items.e: (25 + 15) × 3 = 40 × 3 = 120. Kai’s answer of 70 comes from ignoring the brackets.

items.q: Which calculation has a value of 100?
Freya says 48 ÷ 6 × 2 = 4. Oliver says it is 16. Who is right?
items.e: 48 ÷ 6 × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16. Freya’s answer of 4 comes from multiplying before dividing, but × and ÷ are equals, so work from left to right.

items.q:
Where do the brackets go to make this true?
7 × 8 − 3 + 2 = 49
Which calculation has a value of 24?

items.e: (4,500 + 3,500) × 7 = 8,000 × 7 = 56,000. Not 29,000: that comes from ignoring the brackets.

items.q:
Where do the brackets go to make this true?
6 + 4 × 5 − 2 = 48
Which calculation has a value of 9?

items.e: 900 × 30 + 1,500 = 27,000 + 1,500 = 28,500. Not 1,377,000: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing.

items.q:
Where do the brackets go to make this true?
72 ÷ 6 + 2 × 3 = 27
Which calculation has a value of 50?

items.e: 2,400 + 6,000 ÷ 3 = 2,400 + 2,000 = 4,400. Not 2,800: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.

items.q: Leo says 5 + 3 × 4 − 2 = 30. Isla says it is 16. Who is right?
items.e: 5 + 3 × 4 − 2 = 5 + 12 − 2 = 17 − 2 = 15. Leo’s answer of 30 comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS. Isla’s answer of 16 comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. So neither of them is right.

items.q:
Where do the brackets go to make this true?
40 − 10 ÷ 2 + 3 = 18

items.e: 25,000 − 4 × 3,000 = 25,000 − 12,000 = 13,000. Use known facts: think in thousands. Not 74,988,000: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.

items.q:
Where do the brackets go to make this true?
8 × 7 − 2 × 3 = 120
Which calculation has a value of 1,000?
George says 20 − 8 + 3 = 15. Ava says it is 9. Who is right?
items.e: 20 − 8 + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15. Ava’s answer of 9 comes from adding before subtracting, but + and − are equals, so work from left to right.
8,000 + 120,000 ÷ 4 = 8,000 + 30,000 = 38,000. Not 32,000: that comes from working from left to right without using BIDMAS.

items.q: Evie works out 398 × 52 and gets 2,696. Use an estimate to check. What do you find?
c: It is wrong: the answer should be about 200,000
It is right: the answer should be about 2,500
It is right: the answer should be about 2,000
It is wrong: the answer should be about 20,000
items.e: 398 ≈ 400 and 52 ≈ 50. 400 × 50 = 20,000, so 2,696 is far too small. (The exact answer is 20,696; Evie has missed a zero when multiplying by the 5 tens.)

items.q: A café needs 200 eggs. Eggs come in boxes of 6. How many boxes must the café buy?
items.e: 200 ÷ 6 = 33 remainder 2. 33 boxes hold only 198 eggs, so the café needs one more box: 34 boxes. You cannot buy part of a box, so 33 r 2 and 33.3 do not make sense here.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 6,213 − 2,890?
items.e: 6,213 ≈ 6,000 and 2,890 ≈ 3,000. 6,000 − 3,000 = 3,000. (The exact answer is 3,323.) 9,000 adds instead of subtracting. 4,000 rounds 2,890 down to 2,000.

items.q: Lily buys a book for £4.95, a pen for £2.10 and a game for £6.99. About how much does she spend?
items.e: Round to the nearest pound: £5 + £2 + £7 = £14. (The exact total is £14.04.) £12 just drops the pence. £15 rounds every price up. £140 is ten times too big.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 7,820 ÷ 39?
items.e: 7,820 ≈ 8,000 and 39 ≈ 40. 8,000 ÷ 40 = 800 ÷ 4 = 200. (The exact answer is about 200.5.) 2,000 and 20 have the wrong number of zeros. 160 rounds 39 to 50.

items.q: 30 pupils each pay £4 for a museum trip. The school adds £85. How much money is there altogether?
items.e: 30 × 4 + 85 = 120 + 85 = 205, so £205. £2,670 is 30 × (4 + 85): the £85 is added once, not for every pupil. £119 adds all three numbers. £120 forgets the school’s £85.

items.q: A class has 18 boys and 14 girls. They sit in groups of 4. Which calculation gives the number of groups?
items.e: Find the whole class first, then divide by 4: (18 + 14) ÷ 4 = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 groups. Without brackets, 18 + 14 ÷ 4 would divide only the girls.

items.q: At a cake sale, the cupcakes raise £24. Then 30 cookies are sold at 20p each. How much is raised altogether?
items.e: In pence: £24 = 2,400p, and 2,400 + 30 × 20 = 2,400 + 600 = 3,000, so 3,000p = £30. Multiply before adding. £486 comes from working left to right. £3 has the place value wrong. £24 forgets the cookies.

items.q: A stadium has 45,000 seats. 8 stands of 3,500 seats are full and every other seat is empty. How many seats are empty?
items.e: 45,000 − 8 × 3,500 = 45,000 − 28,000 = 17,000. 8 × 3,500 = 8 × 35 hundreds = 280 hundreds = 28,000. 41,500 counts only one stand. 28,000 is the number of full seats. 73,000 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: 1,030 people are going to a concert by coach. Each coach has 49 seats. How many coaches are needed?
items.e: 1,030 ÷ 49 = 21 remainder 1. 21 coaches carry 1,029 people, so 1 person still needs a seat. Round up: 22 coaches. 20 comes from the estimate 1,000 ÷ 50, which is not accurate enough here.

items.q: 96 pencils are shared equally between 4 tables. Each table shares its pencils equally between 2 pupils. How many pencils does each pupil get?
items.e: 96 ÷ 4 ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12. 48 comes from working out 4 ÷ 2 first. 24 is the number for each table. 16 divides by 4 + 2 = 6.

items.q: Cinema tickets cost £9 for an adult and £6 for a child. How much do 2 adults and 3 children pay?
items.e: 2 × 9 + 3 × 6 = 18 + 3 × 6 = 18 + 18 = 36, so £36. Do both multiplications before adding. £126 comes from working left to right. £75 is 5 × £15. £18 is only the adults.

items.q: 1,250 runners each raise £20 for charity. A local business gives another £5,000. How much is raised altogether?
items.e: 1,250 × 20 + 5,000 = 25,000 + 5,000 = 30,000, so £30,000. £25,000 forgets the £5,000 gift. £6,270 adds all three numbers. £3,000 has a zero missing.

items.q: Grace has 500 stickers. She gives 25 stickers to each of 8 friends. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: 500 − 8 × 25 = 500 − 200 = 300. Multiply first. 12,300 comes from working left to right. 475 gives stickers to only one friend. 200 is the number given away.

items.q: A rectangular garden is 12 m by 8 m. A square patio with 4 m sides is laid in it. What area of the garden is left?
items.e: Area of garden − area of patio: 12 × 8 − 4<sup>2</sup> = 12 × 8 − 16 = 96 − 16 = 80 m². 88 m² uses 4<sup>2</sup> = 8 instead of 16. 92 m² takes away only 4. 96 m² forgets the patio.

items.q: A square patio is 6 slabs long and 6 slabs wide. 5 of the slabs are cracked. How many slabs are not cracked?
items.e: 6<sup>2</sup> − 5 = 36 − 5 = 31. 7 uses 6<sup>2</sup> = 12 instead of 36. 36 forgets the cracked slabs. 41 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: Noah buys 3 drinks at 85p each and a sandwich at £2.40. How much does he spend?
items.e: Write it as one calculation in pence: 3 × 85 + 240 = 255 + 240 = 495, so 495p = £4.95. Multiply first. £9.75 is 3 × (85 + 240), which buys 3 sandwiches. £3.25 buys only one drink. £2.55 forgets the sandwich.

items.q: Harry has £20. He buys 2 books at £6.50 each. How much change does he get?
items.e: In pence: 2,000 − 2 × 650 = 2,000 − 1,300 = 700, so £7.00. Multiply before subtracting. £117.00 comes from working left to right: (20 − 2) × 6.50. £13.50 pays for only one book. £11.50 comes from 20 − 2 − 6.50.

items.q: Alfie buys 4 packs of 6 pens and 3 single pens. Which calculation gives the number of pens?
items.e: 4 packs of 6 is 4 × 6, then add the 3 single pens: 4 × 6 + 3 = 24 + 3 = 27. 4 × (6 + 3) = 36 would mean 4 packs of 9.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 4,987 × 21?
items.e: Round each number: 4,987 ≈ 5,000 and 21 ≈ 20. 5,000 × 20 = 100,000. (The exact answer is 104,727.) 10,000 and 1,000,000 have the wrong number of zeros. 150,000 rounds 21 to 30.
